findings.claim: When fewer than failure_issue_threshold check-ins exist, previous_checkins[:failure_issue_threshold] returns a shorter list and the code still opens an incident. This contradicts the N-consecutive-failures threshold semantics; for example, a new monitor can get an incident on its first failure.

verifier.reason: src/sentry/monitors/logic/incidents.py:48 slices `previous_checkins[:failure_issue_threshold]` and line 52 only rejects when an OK check-in is present; there is no length check, so a new (ACTIVE) monitor with threshold > 1 falls through to set ERROR and create a MonitorIncident at lines 56-70 on its first failure. The logic is a verbatim move of the removed `mark_failed_threshold` in mark_failed.py, so the behaviour predates this patch.

findings.claim: If failed_checkins contains only statuses not in HUMAN_FAILURE_STATUS_MAP, status_counts is empty and the evidence message becomes " check-ins detected". There is no generic fallback, although the docstring mentions one.

verifier.reason: In src/sentry/monitors/logic/incident_occurrence.py:139-156, statuses outside HUMAN_FAILURE_STATUS_MAP are filtered out, so an all-unmapped list gives an empty Counter, skips the singular branch at :145, and returns " check-ins detected" (Django's get_text_list returns "" for an empty list, from memory of Django rather than read here); the docstring's "A failed check-in was detected" at :136 has no implementing branch. The function was moved verbatim from mark_failed.py, and the case is hard to reach because callers normally pass a check-in with an ERROR/MISSED/TIMEOUT status.
